evidence.observation: RestoMart has three founders: Chandramohan R (CEO), Tharun Kumar Rajkumar (COO), and Rajendran Kathiravan (CBO).

Founder profile information identifies Chandramohan R as CEO leading strategy and finance, with IIM Bangalore and Ex-Premji Invest experience; the available founder materials provide role/background information for the founding team.
The founder shareholding at execution is Chandramohan R 5,000 shares (50%), Kathiravan R 2,500 shares (25%), and Tharun Kumar R 2,500 shares (25%), totaling 10,000 shares.
The SHA provides for Founder Directors for so long as the relevant Founder remains employed by the Company, linking founder employment with board representation.
The latest SHA defines 100% of Founder Shares as Restricted Shares subject to lock-in and vesting during the Restricted Period.
The SHA contains founder-related employment, default and transfer provisions that can affect founder share rights in specified circumstances.
The investment materials describe India's food-service market as a large and fragmented opportunity and position RestoMart within that market.
The investment materials identify Chennai as an initial or important target market for RestoMart's food-service procurement proposition.
Product and technology materials identify Chennai as a target operating market for the RestoMart platform.
RestoMart's product proposition includes a technology-enabled procurement and delivery model targeting rapid fulfilment, including a stated four-hour delivery capability.
MIS data contains customer growth information relevant to assessing product adoption and commercial traction.
MIS data contains order growth information that can be used to assess usage and repeat demand.
MIS data provides average-order-value information relevant to customer purchasing behavior and monetization.
MIS data provides fill-rate information relevant to procurement service quality and customer fulfilment performance.
RestoMart's current product is described as a technology-enabled procurement platform supporting restaurant and food-service purchasing.
Product materials describe operational capabilities around procurement, fulfilment, SKU/category management and rapid delivery.
Product and technology materials contain information on technology-related investment and spending relevant to assessing the depth of the technology capability.
Product and technology materials describe a roadmap for further development of the RestoMart platform and operating capabilities.
MIS reports FY25 net-sales information that provides a historical baseline for commercial performance.
MIS reports FY26 net-sales information relevant to assessing current revenue scale and growth.
MIS provides active-customer information relevant to assessing customer adoption and scale.
MIS provides customer-churn information relevant to retention and commercial quality.
MIS provides revenue-concentration information relevant to customer concentration and commercial dependency risk.
MIS provides order-volume and average-order-value information relevant to transaction scale and customer purchasing behavior.
MIS provides fill-rate information relevant to operational execution and customer-service quality.
MIS provides gross-margin information relevant to assessing the economics of RestoMart's revenue model.
MIS provides customer-acquisition-cost information relevant to assessing the cost of acquiring customers.
MIS provides contribution-margin information relevant to unit-level profitability.
MIS provides contribution-profit information and volatility relevant to the stability of unit economics.
SKU-level margin information for H2 FY26 provides additional evidence for assessing product/category-level economics.
Product and operating materials describe the dark-store/fulfilment model relevant to understanding inventory, delivery and contribution economics.
MIS reports FY26 net-sales information relevant to assessing current financial scale.
MIS reports FY26 gross-sales information relevant to assessing transaction and revenue scale.
MIS reports FY26 EBITDA information relevant to assessing operating profitability.
MIS reports FY26 EBITDA margin information relevant to assessing operating efficiency.
MIS provides operating-expense information relevant to cash consumption, scalability and financial sustainability.
The latest SHA states the execution-date shareholding as Chandramohan R 5,000 shares (50%), Kathiravan R 2,500 shares (25%), and Tharun Kumar R 2,500 shares (25%), totaling 10,000 equity shares.

The latest SHA contains a populated Completion Date cap table. Promoter holdings remain 10,000 shares but represent 96.64% post issue, while non-promoter holdings comprise 446 shares, resulting in 10,446 total shares post issue.
Schedule I identifies the investors and their subscription allocations. The listed investor subscriptions total 446 shares and INR 4,125,500.

Investors acting through the Investor Representative have the right to appoint, remove and substitute one non-voting Investor Observer to the Board, with rights to attend meetings and receive board materials subject to stated limitations.
The SHA requires prior affirmative written consent or approval of the Investor Representative for specified Reserved Matters, providing investor governance protections.
The SHA provides information and inspection rights to investors, supporting ongoing investor oversight of the Company.
The Company is required to create or reconstitute an ESOP pool equal to 10% of Share Capital prior to Completion, creating a defined employee-option dilution consideration.
Based on the Completion Date cap table, promoter ownership reduces from 100% at execution to 96.64% post issue, while 446 non-promoter shares represent the remaining 3.36%.
The investment materials describe the proposed/current fundraise and valuation terms used in the investment analysis.
The investment materials contain projected financial information used for assessing valuation and forward-looking economics.
The latest SHA defines the aggregate Subscription Amount as up to INR 2,00,00,000 for the Pre-Seed Series round.
Schedule I specifies individual investor subscription allocations, including the number of shares offered and amounts to be paid.
The Pre-Seed CCPS are mandatorily and fully convertible preference shares with a 1:1 conversion ratio, subject to contractual adjustments.
Pre-Seed CCPS holders receive voting rights on an As If Converted Basis, subject to applicable law and contractual adjustment provisions.
Pre-Seed CCPS holders receive the contractual liquidation preference specified in the SHA, with preference ahead of other shareholders subject to the agreement's waterfall.
The Pre-Seed CCPS carry broad-based weighted-average anti-dilution protection if new securities are issued below the applicable subscription price, subject to the agreement.
The SHA requires a valuation report from a registered valuer supporting the subscription price as a condition precedent.
MIS contains customer-concentration information relevant to dependency and revenue concentration risk.
MIS contains customer-churn information relevant to retention and recurring-revenue risk.
MIS contains contribution-profit information relevant to operating leverage and downside resilience.
Investment materials identify operating and execution risks associated with scaling the RestoMart business.
The latest SHA subjects 100% of Founder Shares to lock-in and vesting during a five-year Restricted Period, creating both founder-retention protection and potential founder liquidity constraints.
The SHA defines Events of Default including specified material breaches, termination of two or more founders, and certain bankruptcy-related events, with contractual consequences.
The SHA contains contractual investor exit provisions, including transfer, exit and related investor-protection mechanisms.
The SHA contains Tag-Along and Drag-Along provisions governing shareholder transfer and exit scenarios.
